messages:
Jamie: Heads up — seeing a 2-3x tail latency spike on prod-dedicated for a subset of Qwen70B requests around 01:20 UTC. Root stack looks like KV eviction churn + kernel fallback, probable when long prefixes + mixed batch sizes hit.
Sam: Can you drop the logs / perf samples here?
Jamie: Pasting quick perf summary I grabbed from the canary: \n```\nperf profile snapshot:\n- 40% kernel_router::choose_kernel()\n- 25% slow_generic_gemm (fallback path)\n- 15% kv_cache::evict() (many small evictions)\n- 10% prefetcher::async_cb()\n- 5% batcher.delay / scheduling\n```\nSam: That smell like kernel selection flipping under certain head_dim/rope_scale combos. Did we change RoPE recently on qwen canary?
Lee: Yep — rope_scale was bumped to 1.2 in the canary to reduce hallucination. I suspect the computed effective rotary dims + head alignment changed, which can force the router to pick a generic matmul microkernel instead of our optimized fast_gemm.
Alina: Also note we rolled qwen KV to fp8 last week (commit abc123). Quantized KV + our LRU+ eviction policy can thrash when long prefixes are reused across many sessions. Eviction -> dequant on misses -> CPU+mem copies -> kernel arrives late and falls back.
deploy-bot: rolled back canary qwen70b rope_scale=1.2 -> rope_scale=1.0 at 01:45 UTC
Sam: Repro I used locally: 1) create mixed seq_len batch (prefix 1024 + live 64) 2) set rope_scale=1.2 3) run sampleprof -> kernel choice flips when effective_head_dim % 32 != 0 and small per-device batch size appears. The router goes slow path.
Jamie: Can we try forcing KV to fp16 for qwen in dedicated to see if eviction churn reduces?
Lee: Short-term mitigations I'd propose: \n- Force fp16 for KV on qwen70b in Dedicated pool (fallback from fp8)\n- Pin kernel preference for head_dim multiples we care about (hint prefer=fast_gemm)\n- Adjust batcher to split big prefixes into a separate hot-cache path so they don't pollute LRU
Alina: For a quick canary I pushed runtime-configs/2001234567-pin-kernel-qwen70b to dev with kernel_hint: prefer=fast_gemm,max_seq=2048. Also toggled kv_precision: fp16 for that pool.
perf-bot: smoke results: tail latency down ~35% on canary with kernel pin + fp16-kv; small-burst throughput regressed ~5%.
Sam: That's promising. We should also add a kernel-router guard: if predicted prefix reuse probability > 0.8 then avoid eviction hysteresis and prefer keeping KV entries.
Lee: Longer-term: implement an adaptive kernel selection that incorporates "expected KV miss penalty" and head_dim alignment, not just raw shape heuristics. Also add eviction hysteresis for prefix-heavy workloads (i.e., avoid evicting entries with high reuse score for N seconds).
Alina: I'll file ENGRT-1428: "adaptive-kernel-kv-coordination" and add perf matrix across Llama/Mistral/Mixtral/Qwen variants (vary rope_scale, head_dim alignments, kv_precision). Tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml.
Jamie: Next steps: 1) revert fp8-kv for qwen on Dedicated (done on canary), 2) land kernel pin to prod canary for 1 hour, 3) Sam/Lee to run synthetic prefix-heavy workload and validate eviction hysteresis design, 4) Alina to own tracking ticket. Thanks.
Sam: I'll run the synthetic tests and push numbers. Adding a small test harness that alternates prefix reuse to measure hysteresis effect.
Lee: Note: the fast_gemm pin is a stopgap — we need the router to choose it automatically once we have reuse-aware cost model. Adding perf counters to the router to learn in prod would help.
Jamie: Agreed. If anyone sees the spike recur after the rollback, ping here and we'll escalate to oncall.
Alina: cc @eng-sre for visibility and scheduling a maintenance window if we need to change pool-level KV precision.
Jamie: :thumbsup:
